# GAPS — symfony-demo audit

**GENERATED by `tools/audit/rank.php`. Do not edit.**
Evidence is under `docs/audit/data/` and `docs/audit/probes/`; the severity,
depth and ownership calls are in `docs/audit/findings.tsv`. `rank.php --check`
regenerates this file and fails on any difference, so nothing here is a claim
without a file behind it.

## Severity classes

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| S0 | **silent wrong answer** — compiles, links, runs, answers differently than php. Ranked above everything because it poisons every other measurement: a green build is actively misleading. |
| S1 | runtime hard failure — crash, uncaught throw, or a `return 0` link-stub that explodes later |
| S2 | compile or link hard failure, or a compiler crash |
| S3 | static finding with no observed runtime effect |
| S4 | advisory / analyzer residue |

**29 findings**: 2 S0, 2 S1, 9 S2, 14 S3, 2 S4.

Capability probes: 1 COMPILE, 6 CRASH, 6 DIFF, 18 PASS (`docs/audit/data/capability.tsv`).

| 1 | S0 | `bare-array-channel-erases-elements` | T2 | repr | THE PLAINEST WITNESS YET for the element-repr root, and it needs nothing exotic: `new W(['a' => 1])` where W takes `array $m` and stores `public array $metadata` reads its elements back as denormal doubles (5.0E-324 is the double whose bits are 1). A bare `array` hint erases the ELEMENT channel by design, so a concrete-element array crossing it is stored raw and read as cells. TWO guards that SHADOWED each other: the erased-ArrayAccess arm fires whenever ANY class in the module implements ArrayAccess (true of every real application), which made the string arm below it UNREACHABLE, and that arm additionally demanded a statically INT index, so it was skipped even where it did run. `$op[0]` worked and `$op[$len - 1]` crashed, which is what made it read as a base-type bug -- inference was right all along (foreach over vec[cell] types key AND value as cells). Now one three-way dispatch on the NaN nibble: object 8 -> offsetGet, string 4 -> __mir_str_char_at with the offset unboxed, everything else the array path. A RAW untagged word stays on the array arm deliberately: there a string and an array are both bare pointers and only an ARRAY is identifiable POSITIVELY (magic at ptr-8), so `not provably an array` must not be read as `string`. WARNING the crash report·s x20 register named the base `starts with`; the `str_starts_with` in the fault address was the ADJACENT constant-pool entry read at base+0x30 as a fake header |
| `psr4-script-hoisted-into-main` | `autoload-semantics` | `docs/audit/README.md` | FIXED, in two halves. composer psr-4/psr-0/classmap are DEMAND-driven -- php reads such a file only when a class lookup resolves to it -- while autoload.files is the bootstrap set it requires on every request. lower_module flattens every file·s top level into one __main, so both ran at STARTUP. (a) A psr-4 file that declares NOTHING can never be autoloaded at all: symfony/expression-language ships Resources/bin/generate_operator_regex.php, a CLI script under a psr-4 root mapped to "", and it is where the tier-2 SIGSEGV actually was; 21 such scripts are skipped in the pinned corpus. (b) A file that DOES declare something still must not run its side effects: symfony/string·s AsciiSlugger opens with `if (!interface_exists(LocaleAwareInterface::class)) { throw ... }` guarding a package tier 2 excludes, and it threw before the entry ran. Demand-loaded files now contribute DECLARATIONS only, and the test is `contains a declaration at any depth`, never `is one` -- a version-guarded `if (...) { class Foo {} }` must survive. Seven files in the corpus carry the guard shape. LIMIT a top-level class_alias() in a psr-4 file is a side effect and IS dropped |
| `closure-bind-scope-ignored` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/closure_bind_scope_static.php` | FIXED. `Closure::bind($fn, $obj, Scope::class)` DROPPED its third argument, and the scope is what `self::` and `$this->` MEAN inside $fn -- php resolves both against the bound scope, which is the entire reason the idiom exists (reaching another class·s private members). symfony/http-foundation RequestStack writes `\Closure::bind(static fn () => self::$formats = null, null, Request::class)`; `self::$formats` is Request·s, lowering read `self` from the LEXICAL class, staticPropRef returned null and the whole program was refused with `unsupported assign target kind StaticAccess`. That single statement stopped the tier-3 build. The closure·s first argument is now lowered with currentLowerClass/currentStaticClass bound to the scope literal (reusing guardClassArgName, which already reads both `X::class` and a string). Sibling of the $this->prop half in emitPropertyAccess: ONE root, two spellings |
| `byref-value-context-no-copy` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/cap_byref_value_context_copy.php` | FIXED. VALUE context on a by-reference return of an ARRAY must yield a COPY -- only `$r = &f()` aliases -- and it aliased instead. The deref handed back a BORROWED word naming storage someone else owns, so the container·s rc stayed 1, the first `$copy[] = x` COWed nothing and appended IN PLACE, and the reallocation left the aliased property pointing at freed memory: implode($h->items) printed NOTHING where php prints the original. Older and broader than the closure work -- the NAMED function and the METHOD forms diverge identically, and tests/aot/cases/byref_method_return.php only ever read a SCALAR in value context, which is why it went uncovered. All four deref sites now retain: __mir_cell_retain paired with the raw-container probe, disjoint by construction (one answers on the NaN tag, the other only on an untagged pointer carrying a container magic at ptr-8), and a scalar matches neither |

## By owning epic

The ladder tier is the implementation order: a tier's dependency closure
lies entirely in lower tiers, so a gap first seen at tier N blocks tiers
N..8 and nothing below.

### `element-repr` — 3 finding(s), first bites at T2

- **S0** `bare-array-channel-erases-elements` — THE PLAINEST WITNESS YET for the element-repr root, and it needs nothing exotic: `new W(['a' => 1])` where W takes `array $m` and stores `public array $metadata` reads its elements back as denormal doubles (5.0E-324 is the double whose bits are 1). A bare `array` hint erases the ELEMENT channel by design, so a concrete-element array crossing it is stored raw and read as cells. Four lines, no union, no closure, no by-ref, no erased receiver -- which makes this the probe the element-repr epic should be driven from, not the by-ref out-parameter shapes it was found through
- **S0** `byref-out-array-element-repr` — the ARRAY an out-parameter hands back reads its ELEMENTS raw. The whole-array repr is settled (the caller's slot is a cell, the call site scratch-and-reboxes), but the callee builds $out['k'] = 10 against a slot typed unknown, so the ints ride raw and the caller — reading a cell array — decodes them as denormal doubles (float(5.0E-323) for int(10)). Same wall from three directions: a string-keyed out-array, an out-array through an erased closure, and a bindTo'd one. Closing it wants the erased ELEMENT channel retyped CELL, which is the element-repr epic, not this one — a by-ref param cannot be retyped in isolation, that was TRIED and broke the self-host build because a closure's use (&$x) capture is a by-ref param that binds an ADDRESS
- **S3** `byref-dynamic-typed-lvalue` — a CONCRETELY-typed local at a by-ref slot of a dynamic (\Closure-typed) call cannot hold what the callee writes — the callee may replace the array wholesale, leaving ints in a slot still typed vec[string]. Refusing at COMPILE time was tried and is far too broad (the by-ref union only says SOME closure declares that slot by-ref, so an unrelated array_diff_ukey comparator was rejected); it now traps at run time on the actual callee's mask bit, before the call, with a named fatal. Initialising the variable to null first is enough to make its slot erased

### `repr-consistency` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S1** `unhinted-static-prop-erased-slot` — an UNHINTED static property (`private static $x;`) has NO single static type, and read and store disagree about the same slot. emitStoreStaticProp NaN-boxes when the declared kind is CELL *or* UNKNOWN, but the READ stays typed `unknown` and the erased read path takes the raw word and guesses: a float comes back as int(4612811918334230528), and a STRING is inttoptr-ed from its tagged word and DEREFERENCED - `self::$x ??= 'v'; return self::$x;` is an outright SEGFAULT, which is the memoise idiom symfony/cache uses to hold its closures. `mixed` spells the same slot and is correct, because it types the slot CELL. Typing the unhinted form CELL to match was TRIED AND REVERTED: it is right for the scalars and WRONG for an ARRAY, which rides RAW through the very same slot, and static_array_prop_append went red at once. The encoding depends on the KIND STORED, so no single type on the read expresses it - this is the unknown/cell erasure root, and closing it wants the element-repr machinery, not a type swap. Severity raised from the original float-only report: it crashes, it does not merely misread

### `sapi-layer` — 3 finding(s), first bites at T3

- **S1** `superglobals-unseeded` — $_GET/$_POST/$_COOKIE/$_FILES/$_REQUEST are always []; $_SERVER carries a CLI shape with no web keys
- **S2** `globals-whole-array` — a whole-array $GLOBALS read is a hard compile error
- **S3** `headers-sent-after-output` — headers_sent() answers FALSE once output has started, where php answers true -- and php then also warns `Cannot modify header information` on every later header() call, which we do not. The out-parameters are honest about the same gap: php fills them with the source position where output STARTED, and no output path records one, so they always read the not-yet-sent values. Nothing tracks the origin of the first byte written. The probe cap_header_emit pins the divergence

### `parser-gaps` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S2** `parser-ref-in-array-literal` — PARTIAL: a reference inside an array literal now PARSES and carries byRef; lowering refuses it with a message that names the construct, replacing an "unexpected token: Ampersand" that pointed at a character and explained nothing. It is NOT honoured, and shipping the parse alone was rejected on the fn-by-ref precedent: an element that aliases is a property of the SLOT, and there is nowhere to record one. ARRAY_REPR_* (bits 1-3) and ARRAY_ELEM_HINT_* (bits 4-6) are WHOLE-ARRAY flags, and RefAddr_ binds a LOCAL to a slot address, never a slot to a source - the same missing fact behind vardump-ref-marker. polyfill-deepclone builds an alias pool it later writes back through, so a copy would silently lose every write. Closing it properly means a REF cell tag pointing at a {rc,value} box, the widen-to-cell machinery already on this branch to promote any ref-taken array element channel, and ~50 element-access emit sites learning to deref - its own worktree and a full gate. The parse-blocked skip in gen_manifest.php therefore STAYS, with its reason upgraded from a parse error to a named refusal

### `spl-classes` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S2** `spl-classes-absent` — PARTIAL: the 10 missing SPL EXCEPTIONS are declared with php parentage (BadMethodCall/Domain/Length/BadFunctionCall under LogicException; OutOfBounds/Overflow/Range/Underflow/UnexpectedValue under RuntimeException; JsonException under Exception). Still absent: the SPL ITERATORS and DirectoryIterator/DOMDocument/ReflectionExtension

### `reflection-tier4` — 6 finding(s), first bites at T3

- **S2** `refl-param-attributes` — ReflectionParameter::getAttributes absent; DI autowiring and controller argument resolution cannot work
- **S2** `refl-param-default` — ReflectionParameter::getDefaultValue/getDeclaringClass absent
- **S2** `refl-union-type` — no ReflectionUnionType / ReflectionIntersectionType
- **S2** `refl-enum-absent` — ReflectionEnum absent; doctrine enum types and form choices need it
- **S2** `refl-hydration` — newInstanceWithoutConstructor absent; doctrine hydration and var-exporter need it
- **S3** `refl-attr-is-instanceof` — ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF is declared but the filter matches exact names only

### `pdo-sqlite` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T6

- **S2** `pdo-absent` — no PDO, PDOStatement, PDOException or sqlite binding exists at all

### `selfhost` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `compiler-must-not-need-stubbed-symbols` — a compiler-side dependency on any symbol that link_stubs.sh stubs is invisible everywhere except the self-hosted build. sha1() was the instance (EVP_sha1 -> return 0), and the failure mode was a SEGFAULT in a compiled program, several removes from the cause. 43 symbols are stubbed in a self-host link — the crypto family, iconv, pcre2 and the fiber asm among them — and the compiler must not depend on ANY of them for a decision it bakes into output. A scan of src/ outside Runtime/Stdlib found no other use

### `platform-parity` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `linux-only-difftest-diffs` — three cases diverge from php on LINUX but match byte-for-byte on macOS: runtime_env, ini_session_defaults, string_gaps. None of them touch anything this session added — they were simply never seen, because difftest had never been run on this branch on either platform. Pre-existing and platform-specific, which per the standing rule (a tier whose finding set differs across platforms is itself a finding) is exactly the class that must not be left implicit

### `error-handling` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `diagnostic-format-vs-php` — difftest flags error_handler_basic and trigger_deprecation_shape, and both are pure diagnostic FORMAT: php CLI emits every notice TWICE (once prefixed `PHP Notice:  `, once `Notice: `) and names the file by ABSOLUTE path, while manticore emits once with the path as written. The suite passes because its expected files encode our shape; only raw php parity sees it. Pre-existing, and adjacent to the no-warnings-throw-exceptions north star rather than a bug under it
- **S3** `function-exists-lies` — NEARLY CLOSED: was 44 of 53 common functions answering false; now 5. Fixed by teaching functionIsKnown the codegen builtins, the rest of the emitBuiltin dispatch and the compiler rewrites. The 5 left are DEMAND-GATED prelude names (error_reporting, register_shutdown_function, set_error_handler, ob_start, ob_get_clean) that the program only MENTIONS inside function_exists without calling — the prelude is then never injected. Measuring caught an over-inclusion too: `print` is a construct php does not expose, so claiming it exists was a regression of its own

### `autoload-semantics` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S3** `autoload-queue-never-drained` — PARTIAL: spl_autoload_register/unregister/functions now exist (prelude/autoload.php), so composer ClassLoader::register() compiles and registers instead of being a hard compile error. class_exists($n, true) still does not DRAIN the queue: the lookup is an emit-time fold into a static table and the guard machinery depends on it staying constant-foldable, so firing it is a design call. Bounded impact — ahead of time an autoloader can never define a class, so only the callback side effects are lost

### `references` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S3** `vardump-ref-marker` — var_dump does not mark a slot that IS a reference: php prints &int(99) for $a[1] after $r = &$a[1], manticore prints int(99). The ALIAS itself is correct — the value changes through the reference — so this is a display divergence, but it is the same missing fact (which slot is a reference) that a `[&$a[$k], $v]` literal would have to preserve, which is why parser-ref-in-array-literal is not just a parser gap

### `language-core` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T2

- **S3** `closure-refmask-module-local` — the run-time by-ref mask for a dynamic closure is recovered by comparing its fn pointer against THIS module's closures, so a closure built inside manticore_stdlib.o and invoked from user code answers mask 0 and passes by value. Prelude bodies are emitted into the consumer's module, so array_walk-shaped callbacks are covered; a stdlib function that RETURNS a closure with a by-ref parameter is not. A global fnptr→mask table would close it and is not worth building before something needs it
- **S3** `dyn-closure-spread-byref-unsupported` — $dyn(...$args) into a closure that declares a by-ref parameter: the spread builds each arity arm's argument list directly and the closure struct carries no arity, so the slot a by-ref parameter lands on is itself a runtime value. Guarded by a named runtime fatal rather than passing the value and dropping the callee's write. The by-name spread arm (a string callable) is refused per-arm at compile time, where the callee IS known

### `stdlib-leaf` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T3

- **S3** `stdlib-byref-arity-vs-zend` — Eight stdlib/prelude functions disagree with Zend about which parameters are BY REFERENCE. This is not a subtle wrong answer: an argument in a by-ref position is a DEFINITION, so a caller writing `f($undefined)` against a by-value declaration has no definition for it anywhere and the FRONT END refuses the whole program (`MIR.verify: dangling local ... read`). headers_sent($file, $line) was exactly that and stopped the tier-3 build outright; it is fixed, these eight are what the same scan found next. str_replace/str_ireplace drop the $count out-param (framework-bundle CacheClearCommand passes it), similar_text drops $percent, sscanf/fscanf drop the variadic &...$vars, stream_socket_accept drops $peer_name; current/key are ours=byref where Zend is by-value, which refuses a literal argument php accepts. Generated by tools/audit/refmask_scan.php, which asks php ReflectionFunction about every global function the prelude and stdlib declare -- Zend answering directly, no table to drift

### `include-semantics` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T4

- **S3** `include-of-runtime-generated-file` — a file WRITTEN AT RUNTIME and then required can never work ahead of time — it is not one of the program's compile units, and no amount of path resolution changes that. Recorded rather than dropped because the original probe was written that way (file_put_contents then require) and a row that vanishes is indistinguishable from one never written. The probe was replaced with build-time-present fixtures keeping both real-world shapes: a file returning an array and a file returning a closure
- **S3** `include-once-repeat-not-tracked` — a REPEAT require_once/include_once returns php's bool(true); under the eager model every file's top-level code has already run inline, so nothing tracks that a unit was entered twice and the repeat re-reads the value slot instead. Bounded: the value is the same one, so only the true-vs-value distinction diverges. Closing it needs the lazy per-file unit model with a _once guard, which changes when every file's top-level code runs and wants its own worktree and a full gate

### `analyzer` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S4** `analyzer-use-function` — the analyzer does not model `use function Ns\name` imports; 10 sites, code compiles and runs

### `regex-surface` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T2

- **S4** `preg-match-cell-boxing-cost` — preg_match $matches had to become cell-element so PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE can hold its [text,offset] pairs; measured 0.088s -> 0.102s (+16%) on a 300k-iteration match loop. Recoverable by specializing on a constant $flags argument, which is compiler work, not stdlib work
